moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Build a reusable, parameterized login group instead of duplicating login steps across tests.
Use incognito mode and conditional execution to make a login flow robust to already-logged-in state.

elements.description: Create and save a shared login group with a meaningful name so other tests can reuse its steps; ordinary grouping alone does not establish cross-test reuse.

Define username/password group parameters and replace the constants inside its entry steps with those parameter references. Caller values can differ. Parameterization alone is not secret encryption or an access-control mechanism.

Remove a recorded Tab/focus step only after checking its effects. It may trigger blur validation or other application behavior. Replay the entire flow and save after confirming needed behavior remains.

bulletPoints: Use a shared, meaningfully named group for cross-test reuse.
Bind entry steps to parameters; protect the credential values separately.
Remove only unnecessary recorded steps, then replay and save.

elements.description: A new incognito session reduces inherited browser cookies/storage when testing login. This does not clear server-side account state or guarantee isolation from SSO and other environmental authentication.

When testing a flow that allows an existing session, use a runtime condition such as login-button visibility or login-page URL. Verify the expected authenticated state afterwards; a skipped login group alone does not prove authentication. When login itself is the test objective, establish a logged-out state instead.

bulletPoints: Incognito resets browser context, not every backend/session condition.
Conditional login supports flows permitting an existing session; assert the resulting identity/state.

examPitfalls.title: Hardcoding one set of credentials into every test that needs to log in
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Duplicating the exact same recorded login steps, with the same hardcoded username/password, across many tests.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a shared group, define credential parameters and bind its entry steps; store credentials through appropriate secret mechanisms.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a test always starts from a logged-out state
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A login test fails intermittently because a prior run's session persisted, so the login button it expects isn't there.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For a flow permitting an existing session, condition the login group and assert authenticated state. For a login-specific test, establish logged-out preconditions; incognito alone does not clear backend state.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a shared login group be reused with different credentials?

options.text: By hardcoding one shared username/password that every test must use.
Define group username/password parameters and bind the credential entry steps to them.
By recording a separate login group for every account.
Credentials cannot be parameterized in Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: Parameters let one group serve many accounts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Parameters must actually be referenced by the group’s entry steps; defining unused parameters does not replace hardcoded values.

optionExplanations.A: A fixed shared credential cannot supply different callers’ values.
optionExplanations.B: The group parameters must be referenced by its credential entry steps.
optionExplanations.C: Separate groups duplicate the reusable behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is incognito mode particularly useful while building a login test?

options.text: It makes the test run faster than any other mode.
A new incognito session reduces inherited browser cookies/storage, helping establish login preconditions.
It automatically fills in the username and password.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about starting from a known, clean state.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A fresh browser context helps avoid inherited browser authentication. It does not reset server-side account state or guarantee every SSO condition.

optionExplanations.A: Incognito is not a universal speed optimization.
optionExplanations.B: A fresh browser context helps reduce inherited browser state.
optionExplanations.C: Incognito does not fill credentials automatically.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A downstream flow permits an existing authenticated session and otherwise needs login. Which approach handles both starts?

options.text: Condition the login group on whether login is needed and assert the resulting authenticated state.
Ignore the failure — it's expected and unavoidable.
Hardcode the test to always assume the user is logged out.

practiceQuiz.hint: Make the test work in either starting state instead of assuming one.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conditional login handles this downstream flow; verify the resulting state. A login-specific test should instead establish logged-out preconditions.

optionExplanations.A: Deleting coverage does not handle session state.
optionExplanations.B: Condition the optional login and verify authenticated state.
optionExplanations.C: Ignoring failure does not establish a valid test outcome.
optionExplanations.D: A fixed assumption fails when a valid session is already present.

quickRecap.value: Shared login group for compatible callers; ordinary grouping alone is not cross-test reuse.
Define parameters and reference them inside entry steps; parameterization is not encryption.
Remove only unnecessary Tab/focus actions; replay to check for lost behavior.
Fresh browser context helps; backend/SSO state remains separate.
Condition login in compatible flows, then verify authenticated state; login-specific tests need logged-out preconditions.
